Question: A list of \(11\) positive integers has a mean of \(10,\) a median of \(9,\) and a unique mode of \(8.\) What is the largest possible value of an integer in the list?
Solution:
The mean fixes the total sum at \(11\cdot10=110\). Thus maximizing the largest entry means minimizing the sum of the other ten entries.

Write the list in increasing order as \(x_1\le\cdots\le x_{11}\). The median condition gives \(x_6=9\). Let \(m\) be the number of occurrences of \(8\). Since \(9\) occurs and \(8\) is the unique mode, \(m\ge2\). Every \(8\) lies among the first five entries, so \(m\le5\). Also, every other value occurs at most \(m-1\) times.

If \(m=2\), all other values are distinct. The first five entries therefore sum to at least \(1+2+3+8+8=22\). The next five, \(x_6\) through \(x_{10}\), are distinct integers at least \(9\), so their sum is at least \(9+10+11+12+13=55\). The ten smallest entries sum to at least \(77\).

If \(m=3\), the first five entries sum to at least \(1+1+8+8+8=26\). Among the next five, each value can appear at most twice, so their smallest possible values are \(9,9,10,10,11\), with sum \(49\). This gives a lower bound of \(26+49=75\).

If \(m=4\) or \(5\), at least four of the first five entries are \(8\), and every entry is positive. Their sum is therefore at least \(4\cdot8+1=33\). The next five are all at least \(9\), giving a combined lower bound of \(33+45=78\).

These cases cover every possible frequency of \(8\), and each gives
\[
x_1+\cdots+x_{10}\ge75.
\]
Hence \(x_{11}\le110-75=35\). The list
\[
1,1,8,8,8,9,9,10,10,11,35
\]
has total \(110\), sixth entry \(9\), and unique mode \(8\), which occurs three times while every other value occurs at most twice. It attains the bound, so the largest possible entry is \(\boxed{35}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
